utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Judge Van Den Wyngaert is unable to sit today. It is expected that she will be able to sit tomorrow, certainly by Monday. In the circumstances, Judge Thelin and I take the view that this is an appropriate case in which the hearing may continue in her absence and an order has been made to that effect under Rule 15 bis. Fortunately, given the technology available to us, it will be possible for Her Honour to view today's proceedings even though she is not here. I believe, Mr. Topolski, we at last come to your opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: And I take this opportunity to make these following remarks by way of opening in the case of Isak Musliu. When asked by ICTY investigators what his reasons were for returning to Kosovo in 1998, a Prosecution witness from whom we shall hear said this: "I just returned to protect the people of Kosovo." Were the people of Kosovo in need of protection? Without a doubt; there had been for Kosovo Albanians ten years of misery under an apartheid-style regime that finally they could tolerate no longer. In the same month that Isak Musliu, then aged 27, a farmer's son from the village of Recak, one of nine children, four of who in due course were to join the KLA, and that same month that he crossed the border from Albania into Kosovo, March of 1998, Slobodan Milosevic invited the radical nationalist Seselj to join his government. Seselj has previously advocated a policy of infecting Kosovo Albanians with the AIDS virus. The people of Kosovo were in need of protection. By the end that same month, the concerted and concentrated efforts of Serb forces were bent on a campaign against both the emergent KLA and the Kosovo Albanian people as whole. The U.S. State Department described it in this way, and I quote: "This campaign is most frequently described as ethnic cleansing, intended to drive many, if not all, Kosovo Albanians from Kosovo, destroy the foundations of their society and prevent them from returning." During the spring, Your Honours, and summer of 1998, the very period covered by this indictment, Serb forces emptied villages of their inhabitants, burnt their fields and their homes, and even slaughtered their livestock. For once, statistics illuminate the picture. In the year of 1998, the year we are dealing with, 1.934 Albanians were killed and mutilated. Of that number, 229 were women, 213 were children, 395 were elderly. There were 2.626 Albanians detained by Serb forces, 41 and a half thousand homes and 1.995 businesses destroyed, 500.000 people forced to flee their homes. Despite the enormity of these crimes, not one member of the Serb forces who committed them has been indicted before this Tribunal, the only persons indicted for any offenses - I underline these words - arising from this period are these three defendants. Milosevic's campaign, as Noel Malcolm observed, was not military but demographic: the uprooting of as many of the rural population as possible. Massacres, massacres committed by Milosevic's men throughout this period will forever fester in the minds and hearts of those lucky enough to have survived them. In its pre-trial brief, the Prosecution say this: "This is not a case," they say, "against the KLA or the Kosovar Albanian people." At the same time, they allege that our client has committed crimes against humanity by virtue of his being party to and part of a widespread and systematic attack on the civilian population. We submit, bold as it may sound submitted, that this will not be sustainable on the evidence, and we further submit now that that proposition is offensive to the KLA and to all those who fought within it and alongside it, by whom I include the forces of NATO. It is our case that Isak Musliu worked and fought in support of the civilian population, not as part of an attach upon it. In Kosovo, this case is seen, we suggest, as one against the KLA and against the Kosovo Albanian people. But we can only urge this Tribunal from now on to have in its mind, which we are confident it will, both the historical and political context in which the allegations in this indictment are played out. Our client remains unashamedly honoured to have served in the KLA, which was not only the people's defender, but as Tim Judah described it, one of the most successful guerrilla movements in modern history, compelled, as someone observed, against their will to talk down the barrel of a gun. Support for that first assertion of ours comes from Sylejman Selimi from whom you will hear, a Prosecution witness, who said this to the ICTY investigators: "Every family were part of the army and the army was part of them." Our client, to us, puts it slightly differently: "We didn't fight because we like to fight, we fought to defend ourselves and the people." That second assertion, that assertion that describes it as the most successful guerrilla movement in history, we suggest, is made out. For how many, Your Honours, how many guerrilla movements have had military the support of NATO? NATO, which flew 33.000 sorties in over 1.000 allied airplanes, dropping some 14.000 bombs and munitions and in that way, for the first time in its 50-year history, resorted to the use of its air force with the KLA in effect acting as its ground troops. The purpose of that campaign, launched as you know in March 1999, chronologically speaking a year after Isak Musliu crossed the border from Albania was, in the words of President Clinton, and I quote: "to seriously damage the Serb military capacity to harm the people of Kosovo." It was to avoid, we submit, that very same humanitarian disaster and not to perpetrate one that Isak Musliu joined and fought with the KLA. In our brief, which the Tribunal would have of course seen, we say this - and what I'm about to read is equally applicable, Your Honours may think, to all I have been saying so far - and I quote from paragraph 9 of our pre-trial brief: "In raising these facts, the Defence does not of course intend to raise a defence of tu quoque. We readily acknowledge that that defence, that is to say that the other parties committed atrocities, is not a defence to a charge of war crimes or crimes against humanity in this Tribunal. It is, however, submitted that in order to do justice in this case, Your Honours must at all times bear in mind the appalling reality of the human rights situation in Kosovo during the time period alleged in this indictment. Moreover, it is of vital importance to understand that some of the evidence presented by the Prosecution in this case will come from members of FRY and the MUP, members of the forces, we say, responsible for widespread atrocities in Kosovo. Thus," and I conclude the quote from our brief, "thus their impartiality and credibility is clearly in issue, as if is any evidence presented by the Prosecution generated as a result of investigations by such forces. So, Your Honours, we invite and urge this Tribunal to give proper and appropriate weight to the political and historical background to these events and may we respectfully suggest to have four matters in mind when coming to consider the Prosecution evidence in this case: Firstly, the extent to which, if at all, evidence presented by current or former members of the forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the MUP is or may be tainted or influenced by bias or worse, bearing in mind that the Prosecution have not only not indicted anyone other than these defendants for events in 1998 in Kosovo, but are also intending to call as witnesses before this Tribunal as witnesses of truth as to the conduct of Isak Musliu and members of the KLA with whom he was associated -- members of such forces as FRY and MUP as, for example, the former head of state security, David Gajic; and Dragan Jasovic who describes himself in his statement as a police inspector responsible for "political delinquency." The second matter which we invite you to have in mind is the extent to which, if at all, those who make direct allegations of criminal conduct and give evidence thereof have been or may have been directly or indirectly influenced to do so. Thirdly, the extent to which, if at all, there has been or may have been collusion between witnesses. And fourthly and finally, the extent to which, if at all, given the rural nature of the locale in which many of these events we are concerned with occurred, there are or may be old scores or old feuds being settled, as opposed to the truth being told. If the Prosecutor is being faithful to her duties under Article 16 of the Statute of this Tribunal to investigate and prosecute persons responsible for serious violations of humanitarian law, it is to be hoped and it is anticipated that she will not shrink from nor allow anyone to leave this building without, if appropriate, further investigation; we shall see. Despite setbacks that have been brought to the attention of the Tribunal on previous occasions regarding the run-up to this trial, our client continues to have sufficient faith in this Tribunal to entrust it with his future. You, Your Honours, will be judging the man. But no one can be separated from his time or his place. Truly, no man is an island. You will hear evidence of the creditable work that he did in and on behalf of the whole community when he served, as he did, for a time as a police officer in Kosovo. I just want to if I may, very briefly, read one or two extracts from material which you are about through Mr. Lehtinen to have placed before you. If either of Your Honours which to follow it, I think believe you have the Lehtinen exhibits that are about to be produced. The file I'm looking at contains tabs 21 to 32. My quotations are only going to be brief, unless Your Honour wishes to follow them with me. The first one I'm going to refer to is to be found behind tab 25 -- in fact, they all are. And the first page I'm going to go to is U0036204, behind tab 25. I hope the pagination is sequential. I think it is. U0036204 behind tab 25 ought to be a Kosovo police service termination notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm going to start where "his police career ended." "His police career ended in May of 2002 on the stated basis that he'd lied, that he'd got qualifications from the secondary school in 1998, when in fact he presented a diploma that he degreed, as they put it, in 2002. So for that lie, he was sacked." But I just want to invite the Court to look very briefly or to hear me very briefly read an extract from another document to be found at a few pages on at 36226 of the same part of the same bundle. 36226. For what we have here are people from his area, ordinary people, asked on behalf of the Kosovo police service what they thought of him. And this - lest it be thought is a partial investigation - this must be being done, given that it is being done in December 1999, at the very least under the auspices of KFOR. In December 1999 as we see on this page 36226, a former teacher, a neighbour, of Isak Musliu describes him as an excellent pupil, never saw him angry. Described at the bottom of that box as being honest and sincere and is recommended. Two pages on at 36228, another consultee, a civilian, a neighbour, believes that the candidate will be able to work with other ethnic groups. He has never committed any violence," I think it means, "to anyone. The candidate can work. At the bottom of that page: "The candidate" - and this is another person who is speaking who is identified by name - "the candidate is very calm and patient. There was no one around like him. No human rights violations. This candidate is respected by all villagers, compared to the police officers in the past, he will be 100 per cent better than officers in the past. He is recommended." The investigator's signature to that document, a Mr. Dermot Wilson and its date, December 1999, is to be found at page 36230. Later on in that bundle - I don't take you to it - one will see and Mr. Lehtinen will show us that be November of 2000 he was being recommended to lead special operations teams. So we invite this Tribunal to delve beneath the surface of this Prosecution's case, however compelling it may be from time to time. For, beneath the surface lies the current, the ebb and flow, of history. In due time and in due course, history will judge the work of this Tribunal. In this trial, Your Honours will Judge the actions and activities of Isak Musliu and his comrades while Kosovo looks on at us all. On the first occasion I met him, Isak Musliu, earlier this year, I asked him what he wanted out of these proceedings. His answer was short, simple, and I quote: "That justice should prevail." Thus he asks, through us, for no more and no less than that to which he is entitled. We know, we know well, Your Honours will strive for both justice and fairness in his case. We are grateful to the Court's patience and for the opportunity to make this opening statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley -- no? Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We are at the point now where you commence your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'm Alex Whiting for the Prosecution. The Prosecution calls as its first witness Mr. Ole Lehtinen. While Mr. Lehtinen is coming in, if I could just say that with this witness I will be using three binders of documents which should have been provided to you; in addition, a booklet of maps and two other booklet entitled "Locations and Victims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you would be kind enough to take the affirmation which is on the card in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Whiting:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Can you state your name.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: My name is Ole Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are an investigator at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you so been employed?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I have been employed here since September of 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long you have been involved in the investigation of this case.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Since I was employed. That's September of 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what has your role been in this case?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I've been one of the principal investigators for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could go briefly into private session for some additional background questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't want to identify the -- or country of origin of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean it will be an extremely brief private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, private session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, without mentioning further the country, could you tell us briefly your background before coming to the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I've worked as a police officer since 1990. I did two years as a patrolling officer. And after that I have been involved in various kinds of investigations as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before coming to the ICTY, did you have any experience in the Balkans?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. I served as a peacekeeper in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and in Croatia during the years 1995 and 1996, and as a international police officer in Kosovo in 2000 and 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the latter tour of duty, what were your responsibilities, briefly?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: As an international police officer, I served in a police station in town called Glogovac, west of Pristina. These were various kinds of police duties and training local new recruits. After that, I moved to the regional headquarters in Pristina where I served as head of regional communications centre and regional office of planning and operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your capacity as an investigator in this case, have you had opportunity to visit the sites where alleged crimes took place?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to draw your attention to a booklet of maps which should be next to you. The ERN on the booklet is U008-3701 to 3710. If you could put the maps on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: One at a time, I guess?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could have the ELMO up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this first map is, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This map highlights Kosovo here, highlights Kosovo as part of the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next map, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This map is a simple map and places and highlights Kosovo in Europe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could go to the next map, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a map of Kosovo with immediate surroundings called "Planning Map, Kosovo, 1998."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And certain villages are identified on this map.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could go to map 4, please. What's shown on this map?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a map that shows the divisions of municipalities in Kosovo as they were during the war, in 1998/1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they change after the war, the municipality lines?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: There's been a slight change in the area of interest. After the war one more municipality was added. It's the municipality of Malisevo which was carved out a few of the other municipalities, Kline, Rahovec and Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I notice there are two names on this map. Could you explain that to the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. On this map there are always two names for each municipality. The name above is the Albanian name of the municipality and below is the Serbian name of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are the brown lines on the map?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The brown lines are significant highways in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does Lapusnik appear on this map?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Lapusnik is marked and has an arrow to the spot where it says Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next map please, map 5. What does this map show?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: On this map, the municipalities of main interest in this investigations are highlighted. There's the six most important municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify them, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: They are Kline, Rahovec, Glogovac, Suhareke, Lipjan and Shtime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, the Albanian name is first and then the Serbian name?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notice there are a number of villages identified on this map. Could you explain the significance of those villages.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yeah. These are villages that are of some interest in the investigation. They are villages that are mentioned by witnesses to be of some importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a scale on this map?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: There's a scale on the bottom. I don't know if it's visible on the screen now, but it's a scale of 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is a box around Lapusnik which is identified as area of image 8.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Later on these map is an image of area 8 and this is area of that image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we go to the next map, please, map number 6. I'm going to ask for the benefit of the interpreters that you pause after my question.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does this map show?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a topographic map of approximately the same area as the previous one. It has the same villages marked on it as on the previous one. The area of this map is from Pristina in the east here up to approximately Malisevo in the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask if we could zoom in a little bit on this map on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this map also have the area of image 8 marked on it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this map have a scale on it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. On the bottom there's a scale of 18 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, using the scale can you approximate the distance -- well, first, could you point out on the map with your pointer where Lapusnik is and where Klecka is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, Lapusnik is here and Klecka is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the scale could you approximate the distance between those two locations.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. I'll use this ruler.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have a ruler there that you're --

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It would be approximately 7 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you approximate the distance between Lapusnik and Carraleve and point that out for us, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, Lapusnik is here and Carraleve is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distance?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's approximately 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on this map could you identify the approximate location where, according to witnesses, Serb forces were located in the spring/summer of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gregor --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection. That calls for a conclusion. You can call me Mr. Gregor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you wouldn't mind standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for a conclusion. Relies on hearsay statements that are not at this point in time been introduced, and invades the province of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That would be a very, very forceful submission were we applying purely common law rules of evidence. The position, though, is that at the moment the Chamber will receive this evidence, but whether any weight, and if so, what weight will attach to it will depend to what extent the question of hearsay is clarified by other evidence and it is shown to be reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I appreciate the Court's ruling. My concern for it specifically is when this witness who is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... who has been called for purposes of dealing with summary evidence is indicating that his conclusions - and it is the conclusions that I am concerned about - is the predicated on unknown witness statements. I believe that it violates a number of serious considerations. And it's for that reason that I raise the objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your point is well-made. It was, though, anticipated, and I propose that the prosecuting counsel be most careful and specific as he adduces this evidence so that we understand what it is this witness is able to speak about and upon what basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I don't think I need repeat that, Mr. Whiting; you've got the message, I trust?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let me back up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, have you had occasion to speak with witnesses who will testify at this trial about where Serb forces were located in this area during the spring and summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those witnesses show you on -- either describe for you or show you on a map where the Serb forces approximately were located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let it be clear that we in receiving this evidence will treat it as merely, in a sense, an introductory summary and it will be of no weight in our view unless later witnesses substantiate the basis for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I appreciate that and that is -- actually will be the case for a good number of questions with this witness, that it will be -- it will be -- in order to situate the evidence and put it into context, I will anticipate evidence that will be coming in later. I will not ask the Court to give what Mr. Lehtinen says about the evidence any weight whatsoever. It's simply to situate and orient the Court with respect to these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That could be valuable if in your questioning you could make clear when it is that you are asking the witness to anticipate his understanding of the evidence of witnesses to follow. That being done, what I have just said will apply to all of that, that is that we will not ourselves attach any weight to what is said about these facts if that does not prove to be substantiated by other evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, keeping in mind my question previously about what you've been told by witnesses who will testify in this case, could you mark with a pen the location that was told to you of Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. And to answer the previous question, I've been shown both on a map and in the actual terrain where the Serb forces were -- approximately were situated at the time. Having Lapusnik here, the white area on the map here is a valley and the Serb forces were, according to witnesses, situated on the east side of this valley. And on this crossroads in Komorane here is where the Serb MUP police had a checkpoint. And that is more or less the line of the front line of the Serb forces at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just so that the record is clear, when you refer to the valley, you pointed to a white area on the map that's between Lapusnik and the line, the blue line that you have now drawn. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you put a mark -- can you -- are you able to see on this map -- well, let me back up for a moment. Have witnesses identified for you where the alleged prison camp in Lapusnik was?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to that prison camp?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see on this map where that alleged camp is located?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This map is not very -- not so clear about those small roads there, but I can point it out more or less where that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a dot where that is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you, using your ruler and the scale, could you tell us the distance between the alleged prison camp and the location of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That would be approximately 4 and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next map, please, which is actually designated image 7.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Can we zoom out a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is this image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is an aerial image of the area of Lapusnik and the village of Berisa and the mountains in Berisa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From where was this image obtained?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is KFOR, which is the NATO-led armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The Kosovo Forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this image on the monitor is sideways, but could you identify what that road is at the top of image which is on the right of the screen.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The top of the image is here and this highway is the Pristina-Peja highway, which was also visible on the other maps. Pristina is here and Peja/Pec is this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you point to the location of the alleged prison camp.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you point to the location of the exhumation of bodies at Berisa.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a scale on this image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This image has a grid which is divided into squares and each square is 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the image come with this scale on it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the scale, could you tell us a distance between -- as the crow flies -- between the alleged prison camp at Lapusnik and the exhumation site at Berisa.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is -- counting the squares is -- [B/C/S on English channel]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a witness during this investigation, has a witness described the route that was taken by prisoners on or about the 26th of July, 1998, from the prison camp in Lapusnik to the execution site in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a pen and draw for us the approximate route on map --

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if I should say this in open session --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually it would be prudent to go into private session, since this is a witness who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Whiting, unfortunately while still in private session there was then a submission against the course that you're now following on the general grounds of want of notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I'll start again. I'll address first the point with respect to the witness. I don't see, frankly, how the Defence is prejudiced if we adopt a course with this witness of protecting his identity. And I would ask that we be allowed to do so. With respect to Mr. Lehtinen's evidence, I am not aware of any rule in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence which require that a statement be produced of a witness -- that a statement be created for a witness before that witness testifies. The rules obviously require that if a statement exists, that it be produced to the Defence. But there is no rule which requires that a statement be created. Of course, there is a requirement under 65 ter that a 65 ter summary of the expected witness's testimony be provided to the Defence. That was done. In addition, this -- we provided to the Defence all of the exhibits that we expect to tender through this witness long -- a number of days ago, more than a week ago now. We produced the list, we produced the actual exhibits at the beginning of the week. Finally, it is my understanding that it is a convention of this Tribunal that investigators are allowed to testify, to put in exhibits and that they are not required to put in -- to create a statement which scripts their testimony beforehand. I said finally, but I will make one last point and that is, I expect a certain amount of commentary with respect to these maps with the understanding that I already described for the Court, that it will be anticipating the testimony of other witnesses who will testify at the trial. With respect to most of the documents that go through, I will do nothing more than, as we said, identify the origin of the documents and highlight certain relevant portions of the document for the Court's consideration, perhaps on occasion, have the witness identify a location on a map simply to orient the Court. In other words, the commentary on these documents is going to be extremely limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Without wanting to go into a full review of the scope of the Rules or of any so-called practices, I think it would be seen to be fundamental to the conduct of these proceedings, Mr. Whiting, that there be notice to the Defence of all material evidence that will be adduced from any witness called on the part of the Prosecution. And whether that is achieved by way of a statement, if one exists, or by a notice of the testimony under the rule you quoted, is not material. Save that, if there is no full statement, the form of the notice would necessarily have to be much more adequate and extensive. That I've mentioned so that there can be no misapprehension for the future of where the Chamber would see the position lies. Now, in respect of the present witness, there is a question which cannot at the moment be dealt with adequately as to whether the evidence that you anticipate leading from the witness will involve matters of significance or not. From what the Chamber has indicated already, I trust it will be clear to both Defence counsel and to prosecuting counsel, that essentially what is being done with these maps could be viewed almost as an extension of the opening remarks of counsel, introductory comments to which the Chamber will attach no weight whatever if there is not other evidence in due course to substantiate what is there. So that we are having what may be seen, I trust, as the benefit of some introductory orientation with the maps. But if the evidence doesn't bear out what is being said, all can be assured that the Chamber will be not acting and giving weight to what is now being said in a helpful spirit by the witness. As the evidence progresses, if the witness is merely tendering documentary evidence and then for convenience of everybody identifying particular parts of it seem to be of special significance, again, there is unlikely to be any particular difficulty. But if the witness should go to other matters and purport to move on to matters of substance, it could well be the result if the Defence of any one of the accused finds themselves embarrassed that there will need to be time allowed before cross-examination so that any embarrassment can be dealt with. Now, is that much clear, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Kahn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And are you satisfied with the position? Don't get too fussy, I'm just giving you --

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it's always dangerous to ask a question. Well, Your Honour, I'm grateful for the way you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't mind having mine pointed out at all. Now, with respect to the question of the naming of the witness, Mr. Whiting, it seems in view of what has been said in the opening, in the course of proceedings so far, that there would be little point in there not being freedom for counsel or a witness to name that witness, because it is very much already in the public arena that the person will be called as a witness. What would appear to the Chamber to be important would be that when it comes time for that witness, the protective measures be in place so that it will not be apparent that this is the witness that had been earlier named at various times. If you would give consideration to that for the moment, we would think if yourself were to name that witness, that would not in itself present a difficulty. There seems to be a technical problem for a moment. We'll pause. Technology has a habit of getting us by the ankles when we least expect it. This has occurred with LiveNote. We will need to adjourn so that the tape can be sorted. And we will take then the break until five minutes to four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honours. It was the intention of myself on behalf of Mr. Musliu to make an oral application pursuant to Rule 73 for an order for disclosure of certain material from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Powles, could I just ask you to pause a moment. I gather that the last moments of what transpired before the break eluded the stalled technology and I'll ask somehow to recreate what it was I was saying in those moments. The point being addressed I believe was to Mr. Whiting, and it was concerning the naming of the witness who we have been mentioning. And the suggestion made by the Chamber was that as that name is already in the public domain from the Prosecution opening and so forth, that it would appear unnecessary to go into closed session whenever counsel or another witness refers to that person. But that it would appear important that when that person comes to give evidence, that there be appropriate protective measures at that time. Now, I -- well, I believe I was in the process of inviting you, Mr. Whiting, to consider that position. And in due course, not necessarily now, that is hopefully tomorrow, to indicate whether you see that to be a practical result. If not, if you could with some precision identify what you see to be wrong with it and what you would suggest in its place. I take it you would like time to reflect on that and it could be done tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Powles, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, it's really in relation to the timing of that application. I'm in Your Honours' hands as to whether you would like me to make that application or at the end of the session -- at the end of the day. I don't anticipate it would last for more than 10 or 15 minutes for both myself to make that application and for the Office of the Prosecutor to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it would be more polite to the witness to continue now. Perhaps we can allow ourselves the luxury of 10 or 15 minutes at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Very grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, during the break I was asked by more than one of the interpreters that, number one, we slow down and number two, we insert a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the break I was asking you about image 7 which is on the screen, and you were about to draw for us the route taken by prisoners, according to this witness, on or about 26th July from the alleged camp in Lapusnik to the execution site in Berisa. Could you take your pen and do that for us now, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I hope this will be visible on the screen, but -- so the alleged prison camp is over here and the witness describes the route as coming out of the -- coming out of the prison and turning right. And along this road -- down here there's a few possibilities of taking paths up along the hill, but it is on the lower side -- on the right side of -- actually, on the screen it's on the lower part of the screen along the mountain, but going up the hill and towards this peak, this is a very significant peak in the area, a big stone. And ending up at this road that is actually a more visible road and continuing along this road. And at some stage which is not fully clear which of these roads it is, turning to the left and ending up at the point which is the execution site.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did this same witness describe -- identify a point along this route where the group met up with a commander?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to the witness, who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That was commander Celiku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you identify on the map the location of that point along the route.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want me to mark this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This crossroads here. I'll make a circle around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to that location?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the grid reference of that location is?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. And I can give the grid reference from the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's approximately 4 -- in an eastern direction, it's 48750, and in a northern direction 471055.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could turn to the next image, please, which is image 8. Could you tell the Court what this is an image of.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a similar aerial image to the previous one. It's a close-up of the part of the village of Lapusnik which is on the southern side of the Pristina-Peja highway which is visible in this upper part of the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this image come from?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is also from KFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this image -- this is identified as image 8. Is this the area of the image that is marked on maps 5 and 6 that we have seen before?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there is a red line on the map. What is that red line?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This red line shows the front line direction of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA troops, in Lapusnik. And I can explain this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you explain it, have you been to this location with a witness who will testify in this trial?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That was Mr. Fadil Qadraku.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he in the Kosovo Liberation Army during the spring and summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he identify at the location fighting positions?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now could you give your explanation, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The alleged prison camp and KLA headquarters at the certain time of the spring and summer of 1998 is circulated with a red circle on this image. The fighting positions were located on this image on the left side of this red line, one facing the Pristina-Peja highway out here in the upper part of the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but just so we have a clear record, when you're pointing to that first fighting position you're pointing to the end of the red line that is in the upper part of the picture?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The next one is very close to this crossroads which is visible on the picture. And then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With -- I'm sorry to interrupt. With your pen could you mark that particular one, that is near the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please continue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Marked with a cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then there's two or three more along this -- actually this -- on the left side of the red line is a mountain ridge and along this mountain ridge is -- the fighting positions are located. And there's two or three more of them along the red line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the right side of the red line, what is there? Just topographically?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Topographically, the red line actually runs along the slope of the mountain. And below, and in the picture on the right side of the red line, is a valley. And on the other side of the valley is where witnesses describe the Serb forces to be positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a scale on this image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This image is divided into the same grid as the previous one, with squares that are 500 metres each.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the grid on the image, could you estimate for us, please, the distance between the alleged prison camp which is within the red circle and the fighting position which you have marked with a cross.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The distance from the alleged prison camp here and this position would be approximately 350 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the scale again, could you estimate for us, please, the distance between the other -- let's say the furthest fighting position.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. The furthest fighting position is in the lower part of the picture at the end of the red line. And the distance is approximately 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are the KLA fighting positions?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next image, please, image 9. Mr. Lehtinen, could you tell the Court what this -- what is depicted on this image, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a close-up of the previous image and shows a smaller area. The directions on this image are the same as on the previous one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is contained within the red circle on this image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Again, the red circle circles the same as on the previous one, which is the alleged prison camp and the KLA headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this map have the same origin as the other images, 8 and 7?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a scale on this map?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Again, there is a grid with squares. And each square on this one is 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could I draw your attention, please, to the road that runs from the crossroads at the top-centre of this image to the alleged prison camp.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. The crossroads you refer to is this. And the road leading to the alleged prison camp runs like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you travelled on that road?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this image the -- that road, is it obscured in parts by the trees. Is -- are there any impediments on that road?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: No. The trees cover it partly, but it's a perfectly driveable road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next image, please. This is designated map 10. Could you tell us what this is, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a map of Kosovo and the immediate surroundings. And the red lines on this map indicate the approximate division of KLA into operational subzones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would -- I should have done this earlier. I would ask that this booklet of maps be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit, as a bundle.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has marked three of the maps or images. It's my intention at the end of his presentation to also mark those as separate exhibits, the ones that he has marked. It may occur that he will have to make additional markings on those images, which is the only reason I'm not doing it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The transcript presently reveals the map numbers in the exhibit, the individual map numbers that have been marked by the witness. I leave it to you, if you feel you need to take other steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just think the markings will need to be in evidence, so we will have to mark them somehow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I draw your attention, Mr. Lehtinen, to a so-called 360-degree presentation, which we have presented -- offered to the Court as D000-1383. It's actually a CD. And I would ask that that be given a number as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a computer presentation of photographs. The witness will lead the Court through the presentation by use of his laptop computer. And I would ask the witness please to bring up the programme on the computer now.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, could you explain to the Court what this presentation is, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a presentation which is done with a special programme by -- of multiple pictures taken in the area of Lapusnik and in more specific places in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it made?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: In the summer of 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain in a little more detail how it was prepared.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. The area of Lapusnik was visited and a lot of pictures were taken, both on the ground and from the air. In specific places, pictures were taken from a camera stand and taken in 360 degrees. These pictures were then, using the special programme, stitched together and -- so that you can go into the image and feel like you're actually looking around in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we open up the programme, I'd like to draw your attention to this booklet of images which is labelled "locations." Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that this be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, what is contained in this booklet?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This booklet shows aerial pictures of the Lapusnik area and specific pictures picked out of this presentation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you open up the programme, please, in the computer.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Okay. Along the way, when we use the programme I'd like to also explain how the programme is being used, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: When an image is showing on the screen of the computer, there are always certain areas which can lead you into a new image where you can then turn around and have more specific views. I'll show it along the way when we proceed. The first image is a simple map of Kosovo, indicating the highway between Pristina and Peja and it has Lapusnik marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And go to the next image, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, here in this image I see prison camp and front line. Are those images you can go into and observe photographs?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct. And at this stage I will show how by clicking the question mark on the lower part of the screen you can -- it actually indicates which areas are the areas that are -- that are possible areas to go and have a closer look at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you go -- click in the prison camp box, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this first image is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is an aerial -- a close aerial image of the alleged prison camp on the left side of the image and the KLA headquarters on the right-hand side of image. The road that we talked about earlier runs between these two compounds right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take us into the alleged prison camp, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking at this first image, what does that depict?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is the main building in the compound, that is, the alleged prison camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've used the word "compound," could you explain for the Court what you mean by that word "compound."

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. What I mean by compound in Kosovo, and especially among the Albanian population in Kosovo, is an area that is usually -- has a wall around it and it has one or several buildings. It can be one or more buildings for living and then sheds and -- sheds and garages and other buildings in the yard. And it's usually inhabited by a family or an extended family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, drawing your attention to the locations booklet which has been marked as P6, could you turn to page 4, please. Is that the same image that is depicted on that booklet?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, does this building look the way it did during the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- there are details that are not exactly the same. I have learned that the buildings in this compound, the roofs and windows were destroyed later during the war. But the foundation of the houses are the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the right of the building in this image, what is that? It looks like a brown gate.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's the main gate leading into the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And leading out to where?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Out to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you look around -- take a look around the yard, please, slowly.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a typical example where photographs have been taken in 360 degrees and you can make a full turn-around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, have you yourself been in this yard?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the location, can you see any of the KLA fighting positions that were identified by other witnesses?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see any of the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you take us into this main building, please, into the entryway of the ground floor and -- maybe this is a good chance -- opportunity to explain how you -- again, how you move to locations.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Again, using the question mark you can see which areas are active for going further in to see details. And whenever the cursor is in one of these areas it will turn into an arrow, and as we can see now, the arrow shows at the door of the ground floor of this building. And this first image takes us into the porch of the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you keep going inside the ground floor, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look around this location, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is the window out towards the yard. And that is the main door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you go back out to the yard, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we go into the first floor of the building, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go to the first floor, I don't know if I am alone in thinking it would be very helpful to know when these photographs were taken. Because we've never had a statement we don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I thought I had asked that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: No, you hadn't. If you had, I hadn't heard the answer, I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, can you tell us when these photographs were taken.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, they were taken during the summer of 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if we could go into the first floor, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Okay. The entrance to the first floor is on in the picture on the right-hand side -- right-hand end of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is the view of the upper floor of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you keep going in, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Keep going in.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now if you could look around this room, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Now we are in the back room of this upper floor. There's two rooms just divided by this wall and the door. And again, the window out towards the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now if we could go back out to the yard. If you would turn and look at the other building in the yard, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to the locations booklet on page 5, is that the same building?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct. And it's marked A2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you go to the well in the yard, the view from the well.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could turn around. Again we see the main building and then keep turning.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the back of the building there, there's a door. What is that an entrance to?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Attached to this building on the back wall is a cowshed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I draw your attention to page 7 of the locations book. Is that the same image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's the same door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you go into the cowshed, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at page 8 of the locations book, is that the same image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you look around the cowshed, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And describe for us what is along the wall there.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Along this wall of the cowshed is a feeding trough for animals and it has a metal bar with chains that are used for chaining animals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to click on one of those hooks and zoom in on it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. One thing you can do in this image is to use the plus and minus buttons on the bottom of the screen to zoom in and zoom out. And on certain details you can also click and get a closer look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you do that, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I'll have a closer look at this chain, animal chain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you go back, please, using -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then complete looking around the cowshed. Could you pause there for a moment. Will witnesses talk about this cowshed?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the significance of this cowshed?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Witnesses will talk about the cowshed. On various times during June and July of 1998, from to up to 15 or 16 prisoners were kept in this cowshed, chained along this feeding trough.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honours, I would be making the objection that I made before with regard to this being a conclusion, with regard to not only who was located in this particular area, but what they were doing whilst in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. But I believe the indications we have given are adequate to deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, do I take it from that that I need not concern myself further as the questioning proceeds in this regard? Because I don't wish to interrupt the flow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wish to make it quite clear at the beginning so that all could be relaxed about it. We're treating this at the moment as merely, in a sense, an opening. I understand technology is producing a problem again. We're operational again. I'm sorry for that. Be content that we are in these respects not treating this as evidence upon which any weight will be placed by the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excellent. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to repeat the last question because it was, I think, missed by the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We seem to be having momentary stalls in the LiveNote. Hopefully it will rectify itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, did witnesses -- have witnesses talked about this cowshed and identified this cowshed?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what have they told you about this cowshed?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Witnesses identified this cow shed as a place where they were held during June and July of 1998. Various numbers of prisoners during various times from two to approximately 15 or 16 prison prisoners. And they describe -- it's been described as they were chained along this feeding trough using the chains used for animals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to pages 9 and 10 of the locations booklet, those are additional photographs from the cowshed?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could keep looking around and then leave the cowshed.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could turn and look at the storage room, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to page 11 of the locations booklet, is this the same image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you take us into the storage room, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to witnesses, what was the storage room used for?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This room is also described by witnesses as a place where prisoners were held at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look around this room, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's not possible in this programme. There's not been a 360-degree photograph made of this one, but you can have a look in the drawer towards the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And drawing your attention to pages 12 and 13 of the locations book, those are the images there?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you leave the storage room, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go back into the yard.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go back to the well.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go back around and go to the view of the garage, please. This garage in this image is at page 14 of the locations booklet, is it not?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the significance of this building?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Also here a witness describes one prisoner to have been held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you take us out to the road between the two compounds, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I draw your attention to page 20 of the book. That's the same image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you turn and show us the front gate of the compound from the road.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's also possible to see the gate from the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show that to us, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that image is on page 23 of the book. That's another view of the same gate to the alleged prison compound?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you take us back and take us into the compound across the road, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is the gate to the compound across the road and I'm clicking at the gate. We're inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- well, first before you do that, this is on page 18, this image of the booklet?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a look around the yard, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This building that's now visible, the white building that is on page 18 of the book, what is the significance of that building?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the gate where we -- the main gate where we just entered is this one and the building -- the white building here is described by witnesses as being the actual KLA headquarters starting from the last days of May in 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you go back to the aerial view, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And back out further.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now could you take us to the front line, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. The area which is active in this programme for the front line takes us to a view that is in this southern end of this yellow line which is marked as front line in the programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what are we looking at in this first image after you click on the front line?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: We are facing approximately north with the Pristina-Peja highway over here. And we're looking from one of the southern-most fighting position towards the north. And the fighting positions were located along this mountain ridge here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the right of the image is the valley?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you take us to the fighting position that is near the crossroads that you identified earlier by marking on a map.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This is, first of all, an aerial image of the crossroads that we were studying earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you proceed, what is the road that is visible crossing this image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is again the highway from Pristina towards Peja. Pristina is towards the right-hand side of this image and Peja in the left-hand direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this crossroads that is visible in the centre of this image, is this the same crossroads that you identified on the earlier images, images -- the image 8?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- are you able to go into the fighting position?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do we see here?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a view from the -- this particular fighting position. At this moment, we're facing approximately to the north overlooking the Pristina-Peja highway again. And you can make a turn inside this fighting position and go towards the eastern direction. And you can again see the Pristina-Peja highway running in the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you been to this location?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you observe anything on the ground from where this -- these images are taken?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. There are trenches and marks of trenches that have been filled in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you were there and you made these observations.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I visited the place on several occasions, but I think the last time I visited was during the summer and fall of 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Komorane visible from this location?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The junction in the Komorane village is over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning, if you would, to image 24 of the locations booklet. What is that image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
