utterances.text: This is an image of the Serb MUP police. It's a checkpoint in the junction of the village of Komorane during the summer of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This image, this is an image from the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning to the next picture on page 25 of the locations booklet, what is that image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's an image of the KLA roadblock in Lapusnik along the Pristina-Peja highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I'm sorry to interrupt. But none of the defendants can see these images if they're not portrayed on the screen. They don't have these booklets we do. I wonder if it would be possible to have this displayed or booklets provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Help seems to be at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: For the benefit of the accused, we're on page 24 of the booklet and now we've turned to page 25 of the booklet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, with respect to the image on page 25 of the booklet, what is that image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's described as a witness being an image of the KLA roadblock in Lapusnik along the Pristina-Peja highway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During what time period?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's also during the summer of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to witnesses, did the roadblock look this way during the entire time?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Witnesses have described it a little differently and individually. Some describe it as a little bit -- having more scrap and iron on the road, like car wrecks, et cetera, but some witnesses describe it as being exactly like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are all my questions with respect to the booklet and to the 360-degree presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: At this time I'll move to another subject which will require the first of the three binders, tabs 1 through 20. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, at the time of the arrests in this case, were various searches conducted?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What locations were searched?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The residences of the accused and the alleged prison camp, the farm compound in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did this occur?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: On the 17th, 18th, and 19th of February, 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the authority to conduct these searches?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It was a search warrant issued by a judge of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For all the locations?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself participate in these searches?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And I was personally present at the search of the Lapusnik farm compound and the residence of Mr. Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the searches of the residences of Mr. Haradin Bala and Mr. Isak Musliu, what have you done if anything to familiarise yourself with how those searches were conducted?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I have had discussions with the investigators involved in the searches themselves. I have studied the material from the searches such as search reports and property seizure records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before each search was conducted with respect to the residences, was an effort made to confirm that it was in fact the residence of the named accused?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain how that was done with respect to each of the residences.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. I personally was present at the search of the residence of Mr. Fatmir Limaj, and we were met by one of Mr. Limaj's relatives who confirmed to us that this was the actual residence of Mr. Fatmir Limaj. The search team leaders of the two other searches have confirmed to me concerning the residence of Mr. Haradin Bala, that Mr. Haradin Bala's wife was present and she confirmed that this was the actual residence of Mr. Bala. And concerning Mr. Musliu, his father was present and confirmed that it was the residence of Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to Mr. Bala's residence, was he in fact arrested from that location?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn first to the search of the residence of Mr. Bala. And I would ask you first to turn to tab 1 in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Am I supposed to have it on the screen? Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. If you could put it on Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could we have Sanction on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to this first document which is marked U003-2411, what is this?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a certificate for Mr. Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to review the property-seizure record for this search to make sure I don't make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would refresh your recollection to view the actual seizure record from the search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have that available. With the assistance of the usher, I would like to provide a copy to the witness, as well as to all the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. I take it that this particular testimony is coming in with lack of personal knowledge based upon what the witness has thus far testified to. We remain in the same position we were in before, as regards to this being an additional opening statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would anticipate at the moment that if Mr. Whiting is wanting it to move into any different category, he will ask questions sufficient to provide a basis for that. In the absence of that occurring, the -- what the Chamber has indicated will prevail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, in fact it is my intention to have the Court rely on this evidence with respect to the -- where items were found, and for this witness to testify about his knowledge from other investigators who did the searches and their records about where the items were found. Of course if there is further dispute about these matters and the actual investigators are required to come testify, we're happy to do so and call them. It seems to me that would be a waste of everybody's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you are proposing at the moment to advance this as hearsay, based upon the information from other identified investigators conveyed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And if there is objection to that, the other investigators relied upon will be available to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, with respect to the search of Mr. Bala's residence, which page of this document that we have is the record for that?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Okay. It's starting from the third page of this batch of documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the leader of that search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That was investigator Pekka Haverinen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he an investigator with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you spoken with Mr. Haverinen about the search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you confirmed with him the accuracy of the record that he made?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this record that you are going to be referring to made at the time of the search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the document that I have asked you about, can you tell from this record where that document was found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. In the yard of Mr. Bala's house, there were two houses. And one of them was identified as a house of Mr. Haradin Bala. On the ground floor of this building there is a room that in the document is referred to by Mr. Haverinen as the lounge, which is a combined living room and kitchen. And in this room on the shelf there was a black briefcase and these documents were found in that briefcase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you asking that of the whole document or that of Mr. Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In fact, of the whole group of documents, which is I believe four pages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The property-seizure records will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P7.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I would also ask for a number for the group of documents that are behind tab 1, which is four pages.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, with respect to P8 could you just read the highlighted portion of the document which appears on the screen.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It says "Soldier, Haradin S. Bala, born on 10th of June, 1957, at Koretica e Eperme in the municipality of Drenas/Glogovac. Now a resident of Koretica e Eperme. The aforementioned is granted this certificate stating that he was a member of the KLA from 8th March 1998 until 19th September, 1999, in the 121st Kumanova Brigade."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, there are behind this three other pages that are part of this exhibit. What are those pages?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Those are similar certificates, and they seem to be certificates for other members of Mr. Bala's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they found in the same location?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just flip through those three pages and identify the dates that those individuals, according to the documents, joined the KLA.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The first has a joining date of 5th of May, 1998. The next one, 18th of September, 1998. And the last one is 13th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning to the document behind tab 2, please. What is that?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is another certificate for Mr. Haradin Bala stating that he was a member of the KLA from the 8th of April, 1998, until the 19th of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this document found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It was found in the same briefcase as the earlier documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next document, please. First could you tell us -- this is designated as U003-2417. Where was this document found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This was found in the same room as the -- where the briefcase that I mentioned earlier was found, and it's in the shelf, in the same shelf where the briefcase was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is an invitation for Mr. Haradin Bala for commemoration of the glorious battle of Fustica 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the commemoration to be held, according to the document?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: On the 24th of July, 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from another exhibit that we will soon see when the battle of Fustica occurred?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. The battle of Fustica was on the 24th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put map 6 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could switch to the ELMO. Could we zoom in just a little bit on -- zoom in, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show on this map where Fustica is located?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have it on my screen -- okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can just point to it.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: There is an upper and a lower Fustica and they are in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while we have this map up, can you identify the location of Mr. Bala's residence.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's in the upper Koretica which is over here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It could be useful, before that map disappears, if there was to be a record at least of one of the villages in the area circled by the pointer as being the location of that battle. I think it was pointed to, but nothing could appear on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, if you could with your pen circle that location of the battle in Fustica.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I don't naturally know the exact location of the battle, but I will circle the area of Fustica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do, thank you.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness has drawn a circle around the area that he's identified. And while we have the map up, if you could put a -- let's say a line under the location of the accused Haradin Bala's house.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could move back to Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I don't believe I gave a number to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could give this exhibit, the invitation to the commemoration, an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving to the next document, please, which is designated U003-2421. Can you tell us where this document was found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This was also found in the house of Haradin Bala in the same room as the earlier documents, and in the bottom drawer of the same shelf or display unit where the other documents were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is again an invitation for Mr. Haradin Bala to a memorial service organised to the memory of a fallen soldier called Jete Hasani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date of the memorial service in the invitation?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's the 16th of October, 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the invitation say the years that Jete Hasani lived?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's 1956 to 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving to the next document, please, which is U004-2422 to 2427. Mr. Lehtinen, where was this document found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a diary of Mr. Haradin Bala, and it was found on the first floor of Mr. Bala's house under a bed in what is referred to as a bedroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are the dates of the diary?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The earliest date of the diary is the 8th of February, 1999, and the latest date is 2nd of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the diary pertain to?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't hear the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the diary pertain to?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The diary seems to be of someone monitoring military movements in the certain area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell from the diary --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I might at this point, I would be objecting. This calls for a level of expertise that this particular witness has yet to qualify for, and is also speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would have to say, Mr. Guy-Smith, if one looks at the content of the document I hardly say that expertise is called for to identify what is there recorded as a record of a military nature. Carry on, please, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the area that is referred to in the diary?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: All I can say about the area is that it's -- the area where this monitoring is done from is -- can see the highway Pristina-Peja in the area of Komorane and Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this be given a number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P12.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next exhibit at tab 6, can you tell us where this photograph was found. Tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's going to be shown on the -- it's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, could you tell the Court where this photograph was found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It was found in the bottom drawer of the same shelf or display unit that -- where the other documents were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: On the photograph, Mr. Haradin Bala is in the middle of the photograph, together with a group of men. And it's a gathering at the memorial of a fallen soldier called Ymer Alushani in Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been to this memorial yourself?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could put image 8 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could switch from the Sanction to the ELMO. And we'll have to zoom out some on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the place where this memorial is located, is it visible on this image?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you with a pen put a circle on that location.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could go back to the Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this exhibit be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next document. Mr. Lehtinen, what is in this image? What is this a picture of?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a closer picture of the same memorial that we saw in the previous picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, this image is U003-4006. What are the dates on the memorial of this person -- that this person lived, Ymer Alushani, known as Voglushi?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It sates that he was born on the 23rd of September, 1964, and died on the 26th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take this image yourself?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P14.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning to the search of the residence of Mr. Isak Musliu. Mr. Lehtinen, if I could draw your attention to what has been marked as Exhibit P7, the property-seizure records. Which pages of that document are records for the search of the residence of Mr. Musliu?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's the first two pages marked U003-7074 and 7075.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the leader of that search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That was Mr. Matti Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you discussed with Mr. Raatikainen the results of that search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you confirmed with him whether this property-seizure record is an accurate recording of the items that were seized during that search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this record, to your knowledge, made at the time the items were seized?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning to the first document behind tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just for the information of the Court, this is obviously a book that the Prosecution will not seek to admit the entire contents of the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Lehtinen, could you tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a book which was found in an -- in what is referred to in the property seizure record as a barn, but which is an outhouse in the yard of Mr. Musliu's residence. And it's a book -- the author's name is Shaqir Bekolli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first three or four pages of this document are a translation of a few pages of the book. Could you read, please, the highlighted portion that appears on the screen.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. "At 1700 on the day before the attack began, that is on 24th July, the Serbian army attacked the villages of Sankoc and Fustica, encountering strong resistance from the KLA and the population. Casualties and losses of military equipment were reported among the ranks of the occupier on the front at Sankoc and Fustica. This attack of the Serbian army (which left several Albanian houses burned) was premeditated, because the major offensive against Lapusnik was planned for the following day. This was out of fear that the KLA forces would attack the Serbian army from behind, but also to draw the Albanians' attentions to Sankoc and Fustica. This could be argued by the fact that at 0540 on Saturday, 25th July, Serbian forces launched a bitter attack towards Lapusnik pass."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would like ask this be given a number, and just to be clear, I don't know what is the Court's preference, whether to put in the entire book. It's the Prosecution intention simply to rely on these first four pages that we have translated, and more specifically, the passage that has just been read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I will look at the Defence table, and particularly Mr. Topolski, whether there is concern that more than the four pages would be of value to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Especially as it didn't belong to my client, there's no concern about it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I already had in my mind, here is a book. Just what the book has to do, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, carry on. We'll find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, it seems that the four pages will be sufficient for all purposes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next document behind tab 9. Where in Mr. Musliu's residence was this photograph found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This was found on the wall in one of the rooms in the main building in the residence of Mr. Musliu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is depicted in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a picture of three soldiers in camouflage uniforms. And Mr. Isak Musliu is in the middle of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to tab 10, please, U003-2566. Where was this photograph found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This photograph was also found on the wall in the same room in the main building of the Isak Musliu residence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: These are KLA soldiers in black uniforms. And also Mr. Musliu is in the picture. And some of the soldiers have the PU badge on their sleeves, which is the mark for military police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that this be given a number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This would appear to be an appropriate time, Mr. Whiting, to have the afternoon break. We will resume at 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: May I proceed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, turning to the photograph that is behind Exhibit 11 -- or tab 11, I'm sorry. U003-2776. Where was this photograph found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was found in the house which is the residence of Mr. Isak Musliu in a photo album which was found in a black briefcase in a room in the main building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: There are KLA soldiers. One is in camouflage uniform. The others in black uniforms. There's both male and female soldiers. They have the UCK/KLA badges, and some of them have the PU badges on their sleeves indicating military police. And some of the soldiers wear a mask.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I recognise the female second from the right as the sister of Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And her name?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Her name is Elmaze Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the photograph behind tab 12, U003-2753. Where was this photograph found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: In the same briefcase as the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a picture of Isak Musliu's sister, Elmaze Musliu, with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you yourself met Elmaze Musliu?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that this be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next photograph behind tab 13, U003-2684. Where was this photograph found?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Again, this photograph was found in the same location as the two previous ones, in the black briefcase in the main building in the residence of Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's a gathering of some men in uniform and some in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anything about the uniform?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. The men in uniforms have a badge on their sleeves indicating that they are TMK members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, please, what TMK means.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. TMK -- the English abbreviation for TMK is KPC, meaning Kosovo Protection Corps. It's a civilian protection corps formed after the war in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: A male person in the middle in a blue suit or gray or blue suit is Mr. Shukri Buja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you met Mr. Shukri Buja?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is he?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Shukri Buja was one of the leading personalities in the KLA in the area of Klecka during the summer of 1998. He was a commander at the point in -- a commander or a deputy commander in the point of Kroimire or Krajmirovce. And later he became the subzone commander of the zone in Nerodimlja.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this be given a number please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P20.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could put map 6 on the ELMO, please. And if we could switch from the Sanction to the ELMO. And if we could zoom in just a bit on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Krajmirovce. Have you been to Krajmirovce?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify it on this map, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Is it on your screens? Sorry. Krajmirovce, or Kroimire, is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a box around that location.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness has drawn a box around the words Krajmirovce, number 6. Now, if we could switch back to Sanction. Turning now to the document that follows tab 14, U003-2577 to 2599.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, can you tell us where this document was found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This document was found in the main house in the residence of Mr. Isak Musliu. And it was in one of the rooms on the ground floor in a shopping bag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This appearance to be a membership card for the Karate Federation of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page on the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe or explain what is highlighted on this next page, Mr. Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This highlights the name of Isak Musliu and the time of validity for this card, which is from the 14th of October, 1998 -- let me see. It says: "Registration is valid for one year." And the first date is 14th of October, 1998. And the second date is 1st of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P21.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just to be clear, for both pages of that -- behind that tab -- rather, all three pages. 2577 through 2579.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the document behind tab 15, Exhibit U003-2833 to 2867. Can you tell us, Mr. Lehtinen, where this was found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. This was found in a brown briefcase in one of the rooms in the main building of Isak Musliu's residence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This appears to be a diary of a man called Emrush Behluli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know it's a diary of him?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It talks about someone in -- it appears that Emrush Behluli in this diary talks about himself and his experiences. It's actually headed "Diary of my life."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 4 of the translation and it's highlighted on the screen, though I'm not sure it's going to be blown up here. Can it be blown up any more?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting at that highlighted portion could you just read the text, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: On 14 June came the first attack on the pass of Carraleve in which the enemy suffered casualties. "On 14th June, 1998, while the Serbian forces were positioned in the pass at Carraleve, Dani crawled by himself to a point 100 to 150 metres from the enemy and successfully attacked them, killing three Serbian policemen. After four hours of fighting, the Serbs were forced to take up their three dead and return to Shtima. The Serbs tried again to break through the Pass but they do not succeed. Every day that they came, they suffered losses."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue on the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: "On the following day, 17 June 1998, while carrying out an attack nearby, my brother Dani was wounded in the right chest, but still continued fighting until the Serbian forces retreated."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, do you know who Dani is referred to in this document?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I believe I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who do you believe it to be?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadan Behluli.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you interviewed Mr. Ramadan Behluli?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will he be a witness in this case, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he describe these events himself?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could -- if you could continue reading at the bottom of page 5 of the translation. And if it could be blown up on the sanction screen.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: "On 26 July 1998, more than 60 tanks were sighted at the Shtima pine trees. They launched an offensive to break through the Pass of Carraleve, but they did not succeed, so then they headed for Sborc. They suffered losses of men and equipment at Sborc. On 25th of July, Ruzhdi Salihu from Sborc died a hero's death."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could this be given a number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen, could you put map 6 back on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if we could switch from Sanction to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the excerpt of the Emrush Behluli diary that you just read, it referenced Carraleve. Have you been to Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you find it on this map, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's over here. It's called Carraleve or Crnoljevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a double line underneath Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go back to Sanction, please. If you can turn to the document behind tab 16 in the binder. Can you tell us, Mr. Lehtinen, where this document was found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This diary was found in -- also in one of the rooms of the main building of the residence of Isak Musliu, in a shopping bag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It appearance to be a diary of Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Mr. Musliu talks about himself in the diary, describing incidents that happened to himself and is referring to himself as the pseudonym Crcizi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 4 where it says "a delayed diary." And if it could be blown up on the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you to read the remainder of page 4 and then from -- most of page 5 and part of page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: "A delayed diary. "Having penetrated in the territory of Kosovo from Albania, somewhere near the hills of Konjushe village, three UCK members came in order to take us in their responsibility... A person nicknamed Hoxha was leading the way to Drenica. We turned" -- an illegible word -- "above the" -- again, illegible word -- "on the right side, and in the evening we came down the hill and reached the Drina bridge. We proceeded towards the asphalt road leading to Camdanica. Having passed one" -- something -- "where the Serb police checkpoint was located just behind" -- again, an illegible word -- "we proceeded with the journey and arrived at the workshop where" illegible "were working. We asked for food and we drank some water. We then asked the owner to help us find a means of transport. We took a" illegible "to Kostove and proceeded towards Kolishan. We were heading in the direction of Likoc. Near the station on the Drina bridge, Afet twisted his leg and we had to take him to the doctor once we arrived in Likoc."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following page.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: "The following day, we went out in the terrain and the psychological, physical, and tactical training started right away. Only a few days later, about three or four days later, myself and Ramiz, aka "Luan", got designated tasks in the area of Silak, and the Shtime" -- and something illegible. "On that night, the so-called "Commander Celiku," Fatmir Limaj, came and picked us up. Together with "Celiku," we went to Klecka where we came across six or seven young men with masks who were UCK members. They greeted us and when they found out who we were, they took off their masks and continued the journey with us. "We entered and, there for the first time, I met with commander Ismet Jashari aka "Kumanova." He was" -- illegible word -- "because he was wounded on both his legs. I did not understand how he sustained these injuries, but what I understood was that we had standing in front of us two men with Albanian heart and soul. This refers to "Celiku" and "Kumanova," what I just said above. I could easily tell the persona behind the person on the basis of their speech and resolute attitude. One or two days later, myself and commander "Luan," Ramiz Qiriqi, were assigned designated tasks in the villages of Stimlje municipality. It's then when I went home for the first time after two years. It is worth mentioning the fact that when we met with Ismet Jashari he addressed me with the following words; 'this nickname,'" -- illegible word -- "'which I had been called by my friends for almost two years and which Luan gave me, 'is not for you. Congratulations on your new nickname -- Qerqiz, because you look like Qerqiz Topulli anyways!' I smiled and said 'Thank you. I can carry it, but I fear this name is too big for me!' We set off from Klecka and arrived in Guncat village in the evening. We arrived at Ferat's house. He was Luan's brother-in-law. They received us very well. A night later, we wanted to penetrate into Qafa e Duhles in the direction of Grejcefc village. We arrived in Bllace village and stayed at Ferat's brother-in-law for several hours. When we wanted to set off for Duhle, as soon as we came out in the yard, firing from different weapons began. It was coming from Duhle. We did not know what to do since we did not know who was firing and what was going on. We then decided to go to Luan's house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to determine what time period is being talked about in this -- in the passage that you read?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I would determine it to be sometime in the spring and -- spring of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is based on what, please?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's based on some separate pieces of information. One is the fact that a man called Ismet Jashari, aka Kumanova, is alive at this time, and I know that he died in fighting on the 25th of August, 1998. And I've learned that Ismet Jashari was wounded in his legs in April of 1998. There's also -- putting this information together with later information about Mr. Musliu arriving from Albania to the area, he has described being in approximately March of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to put map 6 back on the ELMO, please, and switch from Sanction to the ELMO. The passage you read refers firstly to Nekovce. Can you identify Likovc on the map.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you push the map because it's not visible on the screen.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you put -- why don't you put three lines under Nekovce. The diary also describes heading towards Drenica. Can you identify for the Court, to your knowledge, the area that is Drenica. And since it's an area I would ask you to describe it rather than mark it.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I don't know the exact borders of the area that is called Drenica, but people talk about Drenica as an area in this part of Kosovo which -- this white area on this map is a valley and it's called the Drenica valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so we have a clear record. The white area that you're pointing to is the white area on the map which runs from Baijice on the left across to Glogovac.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Glogovac

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then down in a kind of a funnel shape down to Krajmirovce. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you continue.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The mountain area on the left side of the image but on the western side on the map is here. And the area on the north side of the Pristina-Peja highway is called lower Drenica and the mountains on the south side of the Pristina-Peja highway is called upper Drenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could go back to Sanction, please. And if the document -- the entire diary that is at tab 16 could be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to the search of the residence of Fatmir Limaj. I believe you testified that you yourself participated in this search.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Referring to Prosecution Exhibit 7, could you tell us which of the pages refer to that search.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's the last page marked U003-3259.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the leader of that search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: The leader of the search was Matti Raatikainen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This property-seizure record which you have just identified, was that written by you or by Mr. Raatikainen?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's written by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it written at the time of the search?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning first to the exhibit at tab 17, this is a group of photographs. Were these photographs all found together?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where they were found, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: They were found in Mr. Limaj's apartment in the living room in a shelf under the TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just for the record they're marked U003-3239 to 3251. And if they could be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, all the 13 exhibits will be given one number, which is Prosecution Exhibit P24.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the first photograph, and I'll identify these photographs by the number so that there's a clear record. And just the last four numbers are relevant. 3239. Could you tell us what's depicted in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It appears to be three KLA members and two additional persons in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anybody in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the soldiers. From the left is Mr. Shukri Buja. The next one is Mr. Fatmir Limaj and the next one is Mr. Hashim Thaqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already told us about Shukri Buja. Can you tell us who Hashim Thaqi is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Hashim Thaqi was a leading figure in the KLA and he was a member of the general staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next photograph, 3240. Do you recognise anybody in this picture?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. There are three soldiers. On the left is Mr. Fatmir Limaj, in the middle is Mr. Rexhep Selimi, and on the right is Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Rexhep Selimi is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Rexhep Selimi is a prominent figure in the KLA and he was also part of the general staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Jakup Krasniqi also was a member of the general staff and he was also the spokesperson of the KLA, appointed in June of 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next photograph, 3241. Do you recognise anybody in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Fatmir Limaj is here among three KLA soldiers with the military police badges on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next photograph, 3242. What is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: There are five KLA soldiers, two of them females. And Mr. Fatmir Limaj is in the middle of the picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 3243, the next photograph. What is depicted in this picture?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That's a picture of Mr. Fatmir Limaj and Mr. Rexhep Selimi in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph, 3244. Do you recognise anyone in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It's three soldiers and it's -- from the left -- Rexhep Selimi; in the middle, Mr. Hashim Thaqi; and on the left Mr. Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, 3245. What, if anything, can you describe as depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a group -- just a group of soldiers. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph, 3246. Could you describe this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This seems to be a gathering of both civilian persons and soldiers, and seems to be some kind of a memorial for fallen soldiers for the 121 Kumanova Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, 3247.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a picture of Mr. Fatmir Limaj and another soldier, together with children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 3248 -- actually I'll skip ahead to 3251.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: 3251 is a picture of Mr. Fatmir Limaj and another soldier who I believe is called Exhumer Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next document after tab 18. Where were these documents found, please?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: These documents were found in a storage room next to the -- a small storage room next to the kitchen in the apartment of Mr. Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do they appear to be, as a group?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: These are all documents referring to Mr. Fatmir Limaj's stay in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask that these be given a number as a group.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Prosecution Exhibit P25.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the page that is marked U003-3294, which appears now on the screen -- can you tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This seems to be a cheque or a copy of a cheque for Mr. Fatmir Limaj dated in Lausanne on the 13th of February, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to the page that's marked 3296. What is that, please?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a questionnaire with information about Mr. Limaj and his spouse and about their stay in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it -- looking at the highlighted portion, does it say when according to this questionnaire Mr. Limaj entered Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. It states that the date of entry in Switzerland is the 1st of April, 1997, and he's been granted asylum on the 28th of November, 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, 3297. Is there information there which is highlighted about where Mr. Limaj is living at the time?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It doesn't say exactly where he is living but it seems to indicate that he is living together with a man called Ismet Jashari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: I believe Ismet Jashari who was a KLA commander called Commander Kumanova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the same Kumanova that was described in the diary of Isak Musliu?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, 3298 has the date of this questionnaire, which is what, please?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's again dated in Lausanne on the 13th of February 1998, and is signed by Mr. Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the page marked 3301. Are you able to tell what this is?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: This is a rental agreement for, again, Mr. Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the term of the agreement, the period, that is, of the rental agreement?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It's from the 1st of February, 1998, until the 31st of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn please to the next tab, tab 19. These are two documents which are marked U003-3287 to 3289. Can you tell us, Mr. Lehtinen, where these documents were found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. They were found in the same storage room next to the kitchen in Fatmir Limaj's apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are they?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: These are Kosovo Liberation Army communiques numbered 40 and 41.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if these communiques were published in the newspaper?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen newspaper publications of these communiques and they were both published two days after the date on the communique itself. This number 40 was published on the 5th of December, 1997, and number 41 on the 8th of January, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning first to the first page which is marked communique number 40. Could you read the portion that's been highlighted on the Sanction screen, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: "Kosovo liberation Army. For the Media. Communique Nr. 40. Under decision of the Central Staff, the KLA's armed units continued their task of liberation during November. ... "Our armed units carried out other actions of liberation in Operational Zone Number 1 between 25th and 28th of November."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, please. If you could read the end there, again the highlighted portion.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: "We repeat once again to the international governments concerned about this peninsula that our war is a just liberation struggle. The war of the occupier is a war of terrorism. We therefore believe that the time of the resolutions that you vote for, and which lay no obligation on the Serbian terrorists, has now passed." ... "Central Staff of the Kosovo Liberation Army" "Pristina, 3 December 1997."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the next page which is marked communique number 41. Could you read the highlighted portion of that communique, please.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Again, the heading "Kosovo Liberation Army. "Communique Nr. 41. "For the Media." "On the decision of the Central Staff, KLA units launched two armed attacks against the Serbian police in Operational Zone Nr. 1 on 25th of December, 1997: one on a police car in the village of Zakut near Podujeva, and the second in which the police station in Podujeva was hit. On this occasion the enemy suffered material damage..." "Pristina, 6 January, 1998."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P26.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that includes both documents?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to tab 20, can you tell us, Mr. Lehtinen, where this document was found.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: Yes. These two cards were found in the bedroom of the -- of Mr. Fatmir Limaj's apartment in what I would call a beauty box.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to the first card, can you tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: It appears to be a Kosovo Liberation Army travel permit. The name on it is Celiku and it has a photograph of Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the second card, what is that?

utterances.speaker: OLE LEHTINEN
utterances.text: That again -- that looks like some kind of an identification card. It says Kosovo Liberation Army, military police administration and Chief, Fatmir Limaj. And it has a photograph of Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Your Honour, this is an application or a motion pursuant to Rule 73 of the Rules for an order to be issued to the Office of the Prosecutor to disclose the suspect interview of Mr. Agim Murtezi. Your Honours will of course remember that he was the fourth accused who appeared on the indictment with the three accused in this case. He was of course subsequently released and removed from the indictment. So this is an application for the suspect interview that he apparently gave to the Office of the Prosecutor and indeed for any other material in the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor not yet disclosed to the Defence that relates to his arrest and subsequent release. Your Honours, I should say I have of course put my learned friend, Mr. Whiting, on notice of my intention to make this application and he has very kindly indicated to me already that at the moment it's the Prosecution's intention not to disclose the interview transcript or interview details to the Defence. Your Honours, I should also say that the question of such material has already been raised, the general material has been raised before, both in correspondence by the Defence with the Prosecution and indeed at Status Conferences before His Honour Judge Canivell. And it's fair to say that some material but clearly not all of the material relating to Mr. Agim Murtezi has been disclosed to the Defence. I say not all because on Monday during my learned friend, Mr. Cayley's, opening before the Trial Chamber he made reference to the suspect interview of Mr. Agim Murtezi. And it's that that at the moment is not yet disclosed. Your Honours, we submit that the interview and indeed any other material is important and should be disclosed to the Defence for two main reasons and they are as follows. We submit that firstly it should be disclosed pursuant to Rule 68 of the Rules. We submit that it's relevant to the propriety and the manner in which the investigation was conducted in this case. Secondly, we say it's discloseable to us because having referred to the interview and to an extent having relied upon it, we say that the Prosecution have now put the relevance and need for disclosure of the interview beyond any doubt. Your Honours, if I may consider each in turn. Rule 68 requires the Prosecution to disclose material which either suggests the innocence of the accused, mitigates the guilt of the accused, and crucially we say may, and I stress may, may affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence. Mr. Murtezi, like Mr. Musliu, like Mr. Limaj, and like Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond Mr. Bala, was a suspect in this case. He was thereafter indicted alike all of them. We submit that his release suggests that he clearly should not have been a suspect and certainly should not have been indicted. And we submit that that suggests, at the very least, that somewhere along the line during the course of this investigation by the Prosecution there was a very serious flaw. And if that is right, we submit that it's something that the Defence is entitled to know about. We say that because if the Prosecution is capable of making a mistake in relation to one aspect of the investigation, namely the identification of Mr. Murtezi as a suspect and his arrest and subsequent transfer to the Tribunal, we say that there is clearly a possibility that other mistakes have been made in relation to other aspects of the investigation. And it's in that way that we say the details of the mistaken arrest and subsequent release of Mr. Murtezi is relevant and falls under Rule 68 of the Rules. We say that because clearly the material may affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence, in particular the manner and way in which the investigation was carried out. Your Honours have already started to hear evidence from Mr. Lehtinen. As Your Honours know, we have not yet received and are not likely to receive a statement from Mr. Lehtinen setting out his role in the investigation, how he related to other persons involved in the investigation, and where he ranks in the hierarchy of those who carried out this investigation. However, as Your Honours have already heard, he has been involved in this investigation since September of 2002. Moreover, in his 65 ter summary, which was disclosed to the Defence, it said that this witness will provide background -- background to the investigation. Your Honours, if that is right and if there have been flaws in the Prosecution investigation, it would seem that this is the appropriate witness to put such matters to. And it's for that reason that we ask for disclosure of any outstanding material relating to the arrest and subsequent release of Mr. Agim Murtezi before this witness concludes his evidence -- examination-in-chief to put us in a position where we can perhaps consider that material before moving to cross-examine him. Your Honour, the second reasons or basis for saying why we feel we are entitled to that material is because, obviously, the suspect interview was referred to by Mr. Cayley in the Prosecution opening. We submit that having referred to a document or -- and -- or something that's happened, I'm not sure even that there is a transcript of the interview that's been produced, but certainly my friend Mr. Whiting has indicated there may not have -- be a transcript in existence already, but certainly the very fact that he was interviewed, and perhaps there is a video of the interview, I don't know, but having referred to that interview in their opening, and we submit making in a sense part of their case, we would submit the Defence are plainly entitled to have sight of whatever was produced as a result of that interview. During his opening, Mr. Cayley drew attention to the fact that Mr. Murtezi gave a suspect interview and also drew attention to the fact that the three accused in this case did not, as was their right, submit to a suspect interview. We would submit that having referred to the interview and to an extent having relied upon it, we would submit that plainly the Defence are entitled to see the questions that were put to Mr. Murtezi and the responses that he gave. We say that because that we were in a position to ascertain whether the Prosecution were right to refer to an interview in the way in which they did. Your Honours, those are the two reasons why we submit that we are entitled to the interview and indeed any other material not yet disclosed by the Office of the Prosecutor to the Defence. Your Honours, I've tried to be as brief as I can. I see that I may have taken slightly longer than I had anticipated, but unless I can assist Your Honours further, those are the -- our submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just say that on behalf of Mr. Limaj we join the submission put forward by my learned friend, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, we certainly do join in the submission made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: To you, Mr. Whiting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would state first that Mr. Powles was correct in saying that this material has been the subject of prior requests from the Defence. The Prosecution has declined repeatedly to provide this information on the grounds which I will explain further, that there is nothing under the Rules, either Rule 68 or no other rule, which requires the disclosure of this material. It is completely irrelevant. Moreover, I would say that this was told to the Defence on a number of occasions and the Defence could have at that time sought -- made a motion to the Court for the material rather than waiting to the last minute during a witness's testimony and making the motion now. But having said that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we cut to the substance and deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I will. I certainly will. The first -- with respect to the first point, Rule 68, number one, there is nothing in the fact that another person was arrested and later released, which is -- there's nothing in that fact alone that is exculpatory for these witnesses. It has -- it says nothing about the -- whether there is evidence which is sufficient to conflict them or which exculpates them. Secondly, there is certainly nothing contained within the interview itself, putting aside the fact whatever their judgement is about the fact of the arrest and their later release, which obviously the Defence want to draw some attention to and divert focus to, there is certainly nothing in the interview itself, contained in the interview itself, which is exculpatory for these three accused. The Prosecution is -- has reviewed the material, is aware of its obligations, has disclosed all Rule 68 material within its possession, and this does not fall under Rule 68. Finally, with respect to the reference in the opening, as we all know the openings are not evidence, the Prosecution is not going to rely on this information, it is not going to rely -- it is not going to call Mr. Murtezi as a witness. The Prosecution is not going to introduce his interview, it's not going to introduce any other documents. And therefore, it is not part of the Prosecution's case. Yes, it was referred to in the opening merely as background of the case, how we got here, something that happened as -- in the lead-up to this case. It is not part of the evidence of this case. The Prosecution will not rely on it, and there is nothing that is exculpatory for these three accused contained in that material. It is for those reasons that the Prosecution has repeatedly declined to turn over the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, gentlemen. We'll look at this matter overnight and a decision will be given when we resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may make a brief reply to some of the points made by Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES

Identification is an issue in this case and it's in that way that we say all material pertaining to his arrest and Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond subsequent release is obviously relevant to Defence investigations. Second of all, reference was made to the interview by Mr. Cayley in his opening statements, and it's -- we would submit we would need to see the content of the interview to see whether Mr. Cayley was right to refer to the interview in the manner and way in which he did. And we may wish to make comments on the emphasis that was placed on the interview by Mr. Cayley during the opening remarks. Thirdly, of course the Prosecution are not intending to call Mr. Murtezi as a witness, but it's possible that the Defence would like to call him potentially as a witness. And certainly sight of his interview with the Prosecution would assist us in making that determination. Those are the three points I would make in reply.
